title: F-shaped reading pattern in NN/g eyetracking
statement:
NN/g's original eyetracking study of 232 users found that people often read web pages in an F-shaped pattern (a sweep across the top, a shorter second sweep, then a vertical scan down the left edge), so the first two paragraphs and the first words of subheads, paragraphs and bullets must carry the key information.

Options:
- Front-loaded copy: Put the most important claim in the first two paragraphs (or first two lines) of every text block (fits: clear, authoritative, professional)
- Information-first openings: Start subheads, paragraphs and bullets with information-carrying words, since the first two words are read far more than the third (fits: clear, technical, editorial)
- Strong left edge: Left-aligned text blocks with a strong left edge, so the vertical scan lands on meaningful first words (fits: editorial, calm, approachable)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web, ecommerce, corporate sites, search results. Audience: general.

source.title: F-Shaped Pattern For Reading Web Content (Original Study)
